Hope you’re well. Hi Alejandro — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer up front: we do not use customer-provided content from the hosted Redwood API to update or train our public models. Longer answer and some nuance below — I’m looping in Markus (privacy/legal) and Hannah (prod infra) to provide the precise contract and technical details you can share with your security team.

High level:
- Hosted Redwood API: customer inputs are processed for inference only and are not added to the training corpuses used to train our public models.
- Telemetry/aggregated metrics: We collect aggregated telemetry for service reliability and to detect abuse; this is not used to train model weights and is stored in anonymized buckets.
- Private / VPC / on-prem deployments: customer data remains in your environment; Redwood’s control plane does not ingest customer content for training.

I’ve attached an internal retention summary and a SOC 2 pointer. Markus and Hannah — could you confirm wording for our DPA addendum and provide the canonical retention/purge timelines? Alejandro — any specific template your legal team wants us to sign?

Best,

Alejandro — thanks for the question and sorry for the slightly formal reply; want to be explicit for your legal team. Below are concise statements we can commit to in a DPA / Privacy Addendum, plus clarifications about exceptions.

Contractual commitments we can provide (sample language):
- "Redwood does not use Customer Content submitted to the Hosted API to train or improve Redwood's public models, nor does Redwood incorporate Customer Content into any model training datasets without Customer's express written consent."
- "For Private (VPC or on-prem) deployments, Customer Content remains under Customer control and is not transmitted to Redwood’s training pipelines."

Operational details and nuance:
- Retention: by default, request/response logs for hosted customers are retained for 30 days for operational troubleshooting and abuse detection. Audit logs and billing metadata may be retained longer (e.g., 1 year) for billing and compliance purposes; specifics are in the DPA.
- Purge on demand: we can provide an API + legal process to request deletion of Customer Content and associated request/response logs; typical turnaround SLA is 5 business days for hosted customers.
- Telemetry: aggregated telemetry used for reliability/diagnostics is de-identified. We do not use such telemetry to directly train model weights.
- Derived outputs used for product improvement: we will not use Customer Content or derived outputs to train models without consent. We do, however, maintain synthetic and open datasets for internal research; those are separate.

Requested artifacts we can share today: SOC 2 Type II summary, Data Retention matrix (attached), and our DPA template (link below). If Acme needs a bespoke clause (e.g., shorter retention window), we can work through it for enterprise contracts.

Regards,

Hi all — quick technical clarifications to support Markus’ notes. Alejandro, below are the concrete behaviors and admin controls for hosted customers: 

1) Training usage: our model training pipelines are separate from our inference stack. Hosted inference traffic (prompt text, attachments passed to the API) is processed in-memory to generate responses and routed to logging/telemetry only per the retention policy — it is not fed back into model training datasets.

2) Retention windows (default):
- Request/response payloads: 30 days (configurable for enterprise customers to shorter windows via contract)
- KV caches / ephemeral session state: evicted after 24 hours by default, configurable per session policy
- Audit logs (who accessed what): retained 12 months for security investigations

3) Deletion mechanics:
- On a verified deletion request we perform logical deletion of request/response logs and associated indices and trigger reindexing jobs; physical storage reclamation follows within 30–60 days dependent on underlying storage provider.
- For Private deployments, we provide a managed script and runbook so Acme can purge data locally. No data is copied to Redwood training systems.

4) Edge cases & telemetry: we may sample a small percentage of error traces (scrubbed of PII) to debug production issues. Those traces are stored in a separate telemetry bucket and are not used to train models. If you require a complete ban on telemetry sampling, we can put that option into the enterprise config and DPA.

If you want, I can produce a short one-page technical note for your security team that summarizes the above and maps to the DPA clauses.

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
